evals.prompt: Create a draw.io flowchart for a user registration process: user enters email, validate format, check if email exists in DB, if yes show error, if no send verification email, user clicks link, account activated.
evals.expected_output: A .drawio file with a top-to-bottom flowchart using rectangles, diamonds, and terminators with proper edge routing, followed by a COMPLETE Final Report.
expectations: Wrote a kebab-case .drawio file whose XML parses, with system cells id="0" and id="1" parent="0"
The 'email exists' check is a diamond with two labeled outgoing edges (yes and no)
Every edge has source and target IDs that exist on the page and a <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"/> child
Stated the chosen defaults in one line and did not wait for confirmation, because the request names the type and every step
The Final Report opens with a Result: line carrying COMPLETE and the file name
The Final Report has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines; Evidence gives the absolute file path and the N/9 count, and Uncertainty says rendering in draw.io is untested

evals.prompt: Generate a draw.io C4 container diagram for a microservice system with: API Gateway, Auth Service, User Service, Order Service, Payment Service, Notification Service, PostgreSQL (shared by User and Order), and Redis (used by Auth and API Gateway).
evals.expected_output: A .drawio file with a C4-styled container diagram showing all services, databases, and connections with proper C4 colors, followed by a Final Report.
expectations: All six services, PostgreSQL and Redis appear as shapes
PostgreSQL has edges from both User Service and Order Service; Redis has edges from both Auth Service and API Gateway
Shapes use C4 colors (dark blue fills with white text) rather than the Professional palette
No two vertex bounding boxes overlap by more than 10px
The Final Report labels any inferred relationship (for example, which services the gateway calls) as an assumption on the Uncertainty: line

evals.prompt: Make a draw.io swimlane diagram showing a CI/CD pipeline across 3 lanes: Developer (write code, create PR), CI System (run tests, build, lint), and Ops (deploy staging, approve, deploy production).
evals.expected_output: A .drawio file with 3 horizontal swimlanes containing process steps and cross-lane arrows, followed by a Final Report.
expectations: Three swimlane containers exist, and each step's parent is its lane's container ID
Child coordinates are relative to their lane container
At least one edge crosses lanes (for example, create PR to run tests)
The Final Report Result: line gives the container count (3) and the status

evals.expected_output: Asks targeted questions (entities, relationships, flow direction) and writes no file until the user answers.
expectations: Asked about the main entities and relationships before generating anything
Did not write a .drawio file or a placeholder diagram
Did not report 9/9 checks passed or claim a file was written

evals.prompt: Add a Billing Service between Order Service and Payment Service in architecture.drawio.
evals.expected_output: Reads the existing file, preserves its cell IDs, adds the new service and rewires the edges, validates, then rewrites the same file.
expectations: Read architecture.drawio before generating any XML
Every cell ID present in the original file and not removed by the request is unchanged
Ran the 9 checks on the modified XML before rewriting the file
The Final Report names architecture.drawio and says what was added

evals.prompt: Draw one draw.io diagram with all 70 of our microservices and every call between them on a single page.
evals.expected_output: Warns that one page will be crowded and offers multi-page or hierarchical C4 before generating.
expectations: Warned that a single page with more than 50 elements will be crowded
Offered a multi-page or hierarchical C4 alternative and waited for the user's choice
If generation ran, it used the xml-generator, xml-validator and xml-fixer subagent loop with at most 3 cycles
